data.narrative:
Commonwealth Fusion Systems is a Series B2-stage nuclear energy company that has raised $863M to date. The relevant peer universe comprises 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 6 private peers including Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Nano Nuclear Energy, all operating in the nuclear energy sector.

A peer-median valuation method is not applicable here. The narrow peer set in nuclear energy—while totaling 9 comps across public and private markets—does not yield sufficient datapoints when filtered by stage (Series B2), adjacent-stage proximity, or comparable valuation tier. Same-stage private comparables in fusion and advanced nuclear are sparse; applying an all-sector median would conflate CFS with earlier or later-stage ventures and obscure material differences in capital intensity and technology risk. The standard triangulation approach therefore cannot be executed with confidence.

Without sufficient comparable cohesion, this analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. The dataset does not provide multiples, revenue, or capital-efficiency metrics for the peer set that would enable alternative approaches such as revenue-multiple or burn-rate normalization. Further data on the valuation, stage, and financial profile of the five named private peers would be required to construct a defensible range. The primary uncertainty remains the scarcity of exact-stage nuclear venture data; any valuation must acknowledge this methodological constraint and rely on bespoke, deal-specific factors rather than market multiples.
